A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PUN/UPNet research and NUM dataset. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction evaluations, resource measurements, uncertainty-map predictions, training curves, and ablations in Sections 4–5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds environmental robustness tests, real-scene evaluations, backbone experiments, and correlation analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed UPNet architecture, MSE training objective, anchor interpolation, redundancy filtering, and multiplicative uncertainty aggregation remain unchanged in Section 3. Alternative supervision generators and aggregation variants extend experimental checks of the existing framework without revising the default algorithm.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ShapeNet instance/category coverage, v2 evaluates four NeRFAssets objects and four real MIP360 scenes, plus changed-lighting and closer-camera scenarios. Renaming ID/OOD to NUM-inst/NUM-cat and labeling the existing 3DGS evaluation NUM-3DGS-recon do not themselves expand coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Fibonacci-sampling Uniform baseline to both original instance and category comparisons in Table S1. WD, A-NeRF, NVF, and Upper-bnd remain; WD's omission from parts of the main table is a presentation change, since its corresponding appendix results are retained.

E3.justification: v2 states that all methods resample 512 candidates each timestep, whereas v1 assigns fixed candidates to baselines. NUM-inst evaluation changes from ten to five instances per category, and the stated 40-view sampling changes from an 8-by-5 angular grid to uniform spherical sampling. New protocols include every-eighth-image MIP360 testing and alternative reconstruction backbones. These reported revisions do not establish that legacy experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds anchor-count and redundancy-threshold sensitivity tests, a small+add aggregation variant, alternative supervision and reconstruction backbones, environmental robustness tests, view-count curves, and uncertainty/complexity correlation analyses. The original uncertainty-metric, selection-policy, and dataset-diversity ablations remain. v1's training-loss analysis in Figure S2 is removed.

E5.justification: v2 introduces Pearson-correlation estimation and fitted linear trends for uncertainty prediction and viewpoint-complexity relationships in Figures S4–S5 and Table S7. Three-seed experiments and standard-deviation reporting already existed and are retained; no increase in replication or new significance-testing practice is reported.

E6.justification: Legacy reconstruction, resource, and ablation values are retained, while substantial new results cover Uniform, environmental changes, real scenes, additional backbones, and sensitivity analyses. For example, v2 Table 2 newly reports MIP360 PSNR of 17.49 for PUN versus 15.41 for NVF. These are additional comparisons, not performance improvements over v1 under matched conditions.

T1.justification: The interpolation and viewpoint-selection equations retain the same mathematical content, although their formatting changes. Neither version supplies formal guarantees or proofs. Added descriptions of existing mesh metrics and standard complexity measures support empirical evaluation rather than introduce new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction and Discussion broaden claimed generalization from unseen object categories and reconstruction backbones to varied lighting, camera distances, and realistic scenes. This materially expands claimed applicability beyond the original synthetic-object evaluation, while retaining the PUN/NUM contributions and headline efficiency and view-budget claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5.2 and Appendix E explain transfer through a shared notion of viewpoint difficulty associated with geometry and texture complexity. v2 also interprets anchor-count saturation, dataset-generation costs, and threshold sensitivity. The earlier symmetry explanation and image-metric/spherical-viewpoint limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future release; v2 supplies a repository address and reports code, model, and dataset availability. It also specifies mesh-distance units and the completion threshold, plus lighting and real-image selection details. Existing optimizer, preprocessing, hardware, and training-budget information is largely relocated to Appendix C.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive comparison with pretrained occupancy-based active vision, including Smith et al. (2022), and citations supporting MIP360, Binocular3DGS, and mesh evaluation. Application references expand and the environmental-monitoring reference is removed. The central positioning around direct, efficient uncertainty prediction remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative: Section 4's numbered subsections become consolidated topical paragraphs, results are reordered, and training details move into a restructured appendix. Existing captions and discussion passages are condensed or rewritten, and ID/OOD terminology is replaced by dataset-specific names.

P2.justification: v2 combines the original NeRF and 3DGS comparisons into a redesigned Table 1, moves resource results to Table S4, and expands ablation displays. It adds dataset illustrations, view-count curves, and correlation plots, removes the training-loss plot, revises uncertainty-map coloring, and adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow synthetic-object validation through real-scene and environmental tests, a Uniform baseline, backbone controls, and direct checks of uncertainty prediction and transfer. These address important gaps in evidence for applicability and design choices. Reporting weaknesses remain, including five versus ten NUM-inst examples in Section 4 and Figure S1, and geometry/coverage results favoring NVF in Table S5, but the added validation provides a substantial net improvement.
